entry.title: Apple Saved $2.7 Billion in Taxes via Singapore Disclosures Show
entry.content:
Links: ft.com

Apple saved $2.7 billion in taxes this year by routing up to $50 billion in profits through Singapore, surpassing the $2.6 billion saved via Ireland. Singapore has thus overtaken Ireland as the iPhone maker's largest tax shelter, according to recent corporate disclosures.

The shift highlights how multinational corporations adapt their profit-routing structures in response to changing international tax landscapes and regulatory pressures, particularly as traditional European havens face heightened scrutiny.

Expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, the deal is intended to bolster Dropbox's AI infrastructure and support the development of DBX Agent Cloud, a new storage platform designed for businesses and developers building AI models and agents.

The acquisition also facilitates broader AI integration within Dropbox, allowing users to perform file-based tasks using different AI models and connect content to third-party tools like ChatGPT and Claude. entry.title: Crypto and AI Super PACs Lose Majority of Competitive 2026 Midterm Races
entry.content:
Links: citationneeded.news

Crypto and artificial intelligence companies spent approximately $250 million during the 2026 midterm elections to shape future industry regulations, but their super PACs experienced significant defeats in competitive races. Out of twelve competitive races called by early November, industry-backed candidates lost nine, with political action committees investing $74.7 million into losing campaigns compared to just $28.3 million on winning ones.

High-profile losses included the Ohio Senate race, where Democrat Sherrod Brown defeated a record $64 million crypto-funded effort to unseat him, alongside defeats in numerous other Senate and House contests. Despite these setbacks in battlegrounds, the industry maintained a superficially high win rate by heavily backing candidates in safe seats where victory was practically guaranteed.
